cards.back: Says which principals (users, groups, service accounts) may do what with a resource. For search the only question is: may this user read this document?
ACL: the rule lives on the resource. RBAC: on the user's roles. ABAC: a policy over attributes, such as user.region == doc.region.

cards.front: Golden rule for an assistant's permissions
cards.back: Mirror the source's decision exactly: never grant more than the source would.
A Confluence page restriction narrows its space's permissions, so store the effective result, not the raw settings.

cards.front: Groups or users on each chunk?
cards.back: Store group IDs and expand the user's groups at query time. Expanding groups into user lists on every chunk explodes in size and goes stale.
Treat link-shared files as private to the owner unless policy says otherwise.
Filter inside the vector and keyword queries so ranking only sees permitted chunks, then recheck the final few chunks just before building the prompt. Never let a model decide access.
Treat them as their own events that rewrite chunk metadata without re-embedding.
When the permission recheck cannot answer, deny rather than allow.

cards.front: Shared index vs one per tenant
cards.back: One index with filters is cheap and the default for an internal assistant. Separate indexes give hard isolation; use them for external customers and strictly regulated data.

quiz.q: A rule says "readable if user.region == doc.region". Which model is that?
quiz.why: Attribute-based access control evaluates a policy over attributes.

quiz.q: Why store group IDs on chunks rather than expanded user lists?
choices: User lists explode in size and go stale
Vector stores cannot hold user IDs
quiz.why: Expand the user's groups at query time instead.

quiz.q: Where should the main permission filter live?
choices: In the UI, by hiding links
Inside the vector and keyword queries
quiz.why: Filtering after retrieval leaves the model with scraps, and models must never decide access.

quiz.q: A user is removed from a sensitive group. What should the pipeline do with that document's chunks?
choices: Re-embed every chunk of the document
Wait for the nightly full rebuild
Rewrite their ACL metadata without re-embedding
quiz.why: Permission changes are separate events that only touch metadata.

quiz.q: The permission recheck service times out. What should happen?
choices: Allow, since the search filter already ran
quiz.why: Fail closed when the recheck cannot answer.

quiz.q: When is a separate index per tenant worth the extra cost?
choices: External customers and strictly regulated data
Whenever there are more than 100 users
quiz.why: Separate indexes mean a filter bug cannot leak across tenants.
